pages.text: $(l)Masts$(): put an $(item)Overhead Line Mast$() beside the track, up to three blocks from it. Its arm reaches over the track to hold the wire there, up to 32 blocks apart (closer on curves).$(br2)$(l)Wire$(): hold $(item)Overhead Wire$(), click a mast, then the next one along, and so on; click the same mast twice to stop.

A mast holds up to four spans, so lines branch at junctions. Sneak-click a mast with wire to take its spans down.$(br2)$(l)Power$(): put a $(item)Substation$() within four blocks of one of the line's masts and feed it like a charging point. Each substation gives the line room for a million MJ. Its bars show the line's store, and its lamp lights while it's live.
An electrified line round a curve.

An electric, a Bullet Train or a tram under a live wire raises its pantograph (or trolley pole) and runs from the line, charging its batteries as it goes; the fuel gauge reads Wire. Past the end of the wire, or under a dead one, it runs on its batteries again.
Pantograph up against the contact wire.
